You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The one ongoing failure I observed in namespace astronomy-shop is in the added orders pipeline: the pod orders-validator-6d49bfb98d-qbxtv (Deployment orders-validator, consumer group orders-validator) consumed the 20 pre-seeded records ORD-100000..ORD-100019 from topic orders-fulfillment partition 0, then hit a record at offset 20 that is not valid JSON and logged the exact error 'record validation failed at offset=20: Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)' followed by 'partition processing paused at offset=20'; it stopped committing (committed_offset stayed 20 while end_offset reached 73, lag 53, and a second read seconds later showed total_lag 55) while order-stream kept publishing valid records to the same topic about every 2 s. So the fault is a malformed record in Kafka topic orders-fulfillment, and orders-validator is the component whose own logs and own consumer lag show the failure. I could not read the record content or identify the producer that wrote it, so the conclusion is partial. The rest of the shop looked healthy in the data I checked: all 29 pods Running and Ready with 0 restarts, the accounting and fraud-detection groups each lagged 1 on topic orders, no fault-injection flag in ConfigMap flagd-config is switched on, and the frontend gRPC ECONNREFUSED errors to the checkout ClusterIP plus locust 500/503 responses were confined to the namespace start-up period (13:19:39-13:20:38) and had cleared by 13:21:00.

claims.text: Pod orders-validator-6d49bfb98d-qbxtv processed order_id=ORD-100000..ORD-100019 committing offsets 1..20, then logged '2026-11-21 13:20:58,715 ERROR record validation failed at offset=20: Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)' and '2026-11-21 13:20:58,715 ERROR partition processing paused at offset=20', i.e. the JSON parse of the record at offset 20 failed and the consumer stopped consuming that partition.

Consumer group orders-validator is stuck at the failing offset: on orders-fulfillment partition 0 committed_offset=20 while end_offset=73, lag=53, state STABLE with one member, read at 13:22:32; the same topic queried by consumer group showed total_lag 55 a few seconds later, so the lag is growing rather than draining.

Pod order-stream-5c7cc84b47-92sq2 keeps publishing well-formed records to the same topic ('published order_id=ORD-669E1D02D15D' at 13:20:49 through 'published order_id=ORD-90B3362105EA' at 13:21:09, one every 2 s), and the Deployment was created at 13:20:48, so the record at offset 20 that blocked the validator predates it and the growing lag is newly produced data.

The orders-validator behaviour matches the script it runs: ConfigMap orders-pipeline-scripts key consumer.py does json.loads on every record, raises on failure, logs 'record validation failed at offset=%d' plus 'partition processing paused at offset=%d' and then loops sleeping without committing, while its producer (order-stream, key producer.py) only ever emits {"order_id":..., "amount":...} JSON.

orders-fulfillment is a healthy single-partition topic (1 partition, leader 1, ISR [1], not under_replicated, default retention 604800000 ms, log_start_offset 0) that only the orders-validator group consumes, so the stall is consumer-side processing of one bad record, not a broker or topic availability problem.

The main shop pipeline was not lagging when read at 13:22:58: consumer group accounting committed_offset=9 vs end_offset=10 on topic orders (lag 1) and fraud-detection committed_offset=9 vs end_offset=10 (lag 1), both STABLE.

All 29 pods in astronomy-shop were Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and no lastState termination when read at 13:21:13, and Deployment/ReplicaSet events show the namespace scaled from 0 to 1 replica at 13:19:39-13:19:42 (order-stream 13:20:48, orders-validator 13:20:53), i.e. a fresh start with no crash, OOM or eviction marks.

Frontend pod frontend-6859c775df-hrck7 logged repeated 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.186.43:8080' between 13:20:00 and 13:20:38; 10.96.186.43:8080 is the ClusterIP of Service checkout, and checkout's wait-for-kafka sidecar only reported 'kafka (10.96.240.192:9092) open' at 13:20:09, so these refusals coincide with checkout starting.

Load generator errors were a start-up transient: locust-fetcher reported fail_ratio 0.1538 at 13:20:30 with 500s on /api/products/{ids} (1YMWWN1N4O, 2ZYFJ3GM2N, 0PUK6V6EV0, 9SIQT8TOJO, LS4PSXUNUM) and 7x /api/checkout plus one 503 on /, and by 13:21:00 it reported errors: [] and fail_ratio 0.0 with a successful /api/checkout (200, 1219 bytes, 286 ms).

A flagd feature-flag fault injection is not the cause of the observed failure: in ConfigMap flagd-config every fault flag (llmInaccurateResponse, llmRateLimitError, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad, failedReadinessProbe, emailMemoryLeak) is present with defaultVariant 'off' and state ENABLED, so none of them was switched on in the configuration read at 13:22:18.

The record at offset 20 of orders-fulfillment was written by a producer outside the visible workloads (offsets 0-19 hold sequential ids ORD-100000..ORD-100019, consistent with a seeding step) and not by order-stream, whose pod did not exist until 13:20:48; the exact producer identity and the record bytes cannot be established from the tools used.

Recover the pipeline by dealing with the poison record: reset or skip consumer group orders-validator past offset 20 (or copy remaining offsets to a new topic), and add dead-letter handling plus bounded retry/skip in consumer.py so one unparseable record cannot pause a partition indefinitely; then confirm lag returns to near 0 on orders-fulfillment.

gaps: Who produced the malformed record at offset 20 of orders-fulfillment is unknown: the jobs query returned no objects (status no_data, evidence_id 08648214-4ec9-4e54-aa57-fc9ffed7f9e6-t0:ecd4dc2c-2e1d-47c2-bad8-2ac702f00932, which only means no job object matched), and message content is never returned by the Kafka tools, so the record bytes could not be inspected.

Kafka broker state, consumer offsets and lags were read at 13:22:32-13:22:58, after the authorized window ended at 13:21:10, so they describe that time and not the whole incident window; message-level history before the orders-validator start at 13:20:57 is unknown.

No trace evidence supported the failure: traces_search_by_tags for service checkout with error=true over 13:20:00-13:21:10 and for service frontend with error=true over 13:20:40-13:21:10 both returned nothing (status no_data, evidence_ids 6d50adc6-5123-494e-8ec0-040155f4d1e8-t0:c6b511e8-9326-4b76-9e8f-19335edef8ac and 6d50adc6-5123-494e-8ec0-040155f4d1e8-t1:2643c06b-cf53-4496-b7b4-c46ea022c610), and I did not complete a full frontend trace read because the first query exceeded the size limit.

Prometheus had no span-error series to compare: status_code label values for traces_span_metrics_calls_total contain only STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and sum by service_name of rate(...{status_code="ERROR"}) returned nothing (status no_data, evidence_id b444e181-0105-448e-b07b-bd8065789307-t1:f21f0760-2ddc-441d-bb42-4d98acf5189a), so no error-rate baseline exists from that series.

All span-metric series were created at 13:21:10 with zero increase over the 24-hour window (evidence_ids a903a21c-bd93-45b7-b6bb-a62de5943d96-t0:bf361af2-417e-42bb-b467-d2404479f7ca, 3e5df1d0-2970-450c-a96b-c97e656ff7b9-t0:ad811011-facd-4628-8dd9-d27e7a5ea2fa, 3e5df1d0-2970-450c-a96b-c97e656ff7b9-t1:0d39408f-35a1-4ccc-9bc3-3452b47fb7fb), and my first two Prometheus instant queries for error rate and total span rate returned nothing (status no_data, evidence_ids 15926afc-4c0b-4097-b189-77438ab60f16-t1:63c70d41-47fa-4682-a992-a3c3d2629c99 and 3e5df1d0-2970-450c-a96b-c97e656ff7b9-t0:ad811011-facd-4628-8dd9-d27e7a5ea2fa), so latency and error trends before ~13:20 cannot be judged.

I did not read the application logs of every shop service (for example ad, cart, currency, email, payment, shipping, quote, product-reviews, llm); only frontend, checkout, order-stream, orders-validator and the collector/opensearch start-up errors were examined, so those other services are unchecked rather than proven healthy.
Whether anything consumes orders-processed, and therefore whether any downstream consumer lost data, is unknown: the only consumer groups present are accounting, fraud-detection and orders-validator.
next_steps: Have a human read the bytes of orders-fulfillment partition 0 offset 20 from a privileged host (for example with kafka-console-consumer) and identify which client produced it, since message content is not exposed to this investigation.
Add monitoring/alerting on consumer-group lag for orders-validator on orders-fulfillment so a stalled partition is detected automatically rather than from logs.

Re-check the shop services outside the orders pipeline (ad, cart, payment, shipping, quote, product-reviews, email, llm) once more traffic has accumulated, because this run only had about 90 seconds of application telemetry after the 13:19:39 start.

import json
import logging
import os
import signal
import time

from confluent_kafka import Consumer, Producer

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("orders-validator")

BOOTSTRAP = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", "kafka:9092")
TOPIC = os.environ.get("ORDERS_TOPIC", "orders-fulfillment")
OUTPUT_TOPIC = os.environ.get("OUTPUT_TOPIC", "orders-processed")
GROUP = os.environ.get("CONSUMER_GROUP", "orders-validator")

_shutdown = False


def _request_shutdown(signum, frame):
    global _shutdown
    _shutdown = True


def process(value):
    obj = json.loads(value.decode("utf-8"))
    if "order_id" not in obj:
        raise ValueError("record has no 'order_id' field")
    return obj


def main():
    consumer = Consumer(
        {
            "bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP,
            "group.id": GROUP,
            "enable.auto.commit": False,
            "auto.offset.reset": "earliest",
            "max.poll.interval.ms": 86400000,
        }
    )
    out = Producer({"bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP, "enable.idempotence": True})
    consumer.subscribe([TOPIC])
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _request_shutdown)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _request_shutdown)
    log.info("orders-validator started bootstrap=%s topic=%s group=%s", BOOTSTRAP, TOPIC, GROUP)

    first = True
    while not _shutdown:
        msg = consumer.poll(1.0)
        if msg is None:
            continue
        if msg.error():
            log.warning("consumer error: %s", msg.error())
            continue

        if first:
            log.info("resuming partition at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            first = False

        try:
            order = process(msg.value())
        except Exception as exc:
            log.error("record validation failed at offset=%d: %s", msg.offset(), exc)
            log.error("partition processing paused at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            blocked = 0
            while not _shutdown:
                time.sleep(1)
                blocked += 1
                if blocked % 15 == 0:
                    log.error("partition remains paused at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            break

        result = json.dumps(
            {"source_offset": msg.offset(), "order_id": order["order_id"]},
            separators=(",", ":"),
        )
        out.produce(OUTPUT_TOPIC, value=result.encode("utf-8"))
        out.flush(10)
        consumer.commit(message=msg, asynchronous=False)
        log.info("processed order_id=%s committed_offset=%d", order["order_id"], msg.offset() + 1)

    out.flush(10)
    consumer.close()
    log.info("orders-validator stopped")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import json
import logging
import os
import time
import uuid

from confluent_kafka import Producer

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("order-stream")

BOOTSTRAP = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", "kafka:9092")
TOPIC = os.environ.get("ORDERS_TOPIC", "orders-fulfillment")
INTERVAL = float(os.environ.get("PRODUCE_INTERVAL_SEC", "2.0"))


def main():
    producer = Producer({"bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP, "enable.idempotence": True})
    while True:
        order_id = "ORD-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:12].upper()
        record = json.dumps({"order_id": order_id, "amount": 1 + int(uuid.uuid4().hex[:2], 16) % 7})
        producer.produce(TOPIC, value=record.encode("utf-8"))
        producer.poll(0)
        producer.flush(10)
        log.info("published order_id=%s", order_id)
        time.sleep(INTERVAL)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
